arith_reference: runtime.reference.formats binary32_add, binary32_multiply and binary32_bits_to_bf16_rne, plus binary32_product_add for exact BF16 products accumulated with one final binary32 RNE rounding; all compute with fractions.Fraction, so no host floating-point mode participates

cases.name: matmul_bf16_small
cases.note: 4 x 16 activations against 8 x 16 weights: the ordinary contraction

cases.name: matmul_bf16_tile_edge
cases.note: 9 x 33 against 65 x 33: crosses the frozen kernel's 8-row and 64-column work tile in both directions, so a tiling that leaked into the arithmetic would show here

cases.name: matmul_bf16_saturating
cases.note: an accumulator that stays inside binary32 and leaves the BF16 range: six of twelve outputs saturate to the largest finite code, and the saturation is counted rather than raised

cases.name: matmul_bf16_signed_zero
cases.note: every product is an exact zero of one sign or the other: the contract canonicalises them positive before accumulation, so the result must be +0 and not -0

cases.name: matmul_bf16_reduction_order
cases.note: a contraction whose BF16 output distinguishes ascending-K from any other association: a small leading product, then an exact cancellation of two large ones.  Ascending absorbs the small term and returns zero; any order that cancels first returns it whole

cases.name: matmul_fp8_reduction_order
cases.note: the same order-sensitive construction on the FP8 path, which reaches runtime.sim.backend.sequential_matmul_binary32 rather than the frozen BF16 kernel -- two separate implementations of one contract, so both need an operand set that can see the order

cases.name: matmul_bf16_wide_reduction
cases.note: a 256-deep reduction, where an association error accumulates instead of cancelling

cases.name: matmul_fp8_fp8
cases.note: FP8 E4M3FN on both sides: exact decode, exact products, the same ascending-K binary32 reduction

cases.name: matmul_fp8_k_major_schedule
cases.note: 64 x 128 output over a 4-deep reduction: 8,192 output elements is exactly the tile at which runtime.sim.backend switches the sequential contraction from its K-last schedule to its K-major one.  The contract says the two agree bit for bit; this case is where the RTL checks that claim against the other schedule

cases.name: matmul_mxfp4_fp8_block_scaled
cases.note: the pair the released DeepSeek MoE actually ships: MXFP4 E2M1 activations and FP8 E4M3FN weights, each with its own 32-element E8M0 block scale.  Amendment A8's one-dimensional block

cases.name: matmul_fp8_a15_block_rows
cases.note: amendment A15's two-dimensional scale block: one E8M0 code per 4 x 32 tile of the weight, which is the shape the released DeepSeek FP8 linears use and the shape an A8-only reader addresses wrongly

cases.golden_message: bf16_bf16_fp32_sequential_rne_v1: input_codes contains BF16 NaN or infinity
cases.name: matmul_bf16_operand_nonfinite
cases.note: a BF16 infinity in the activation: the contraction is refused and the destination is left untouched

cases.golden_message: weight view 4 contains 1 reserved or NaN FP8_E4M3FN encoding(s)
cases.name: matmul_fp8_reserved_encoding
cases.note: the reserved E4M3FN encoding 0x7f is a poisoned block, not a value

cases.name: matmul_bf16_product_overflow
cases.note: the largest finite BF16 squared leaves the binary32 range.  The offending product is the first reduction index of the first output element, which is where the two refusal orders coincide -- see the campaign's claim boundary

cases.name: matmul_bf16_accumulate_overflow
cases.note: every product is finite and their ascending-K sum is not: 2**63 squared is 2**126, and four of them overflow binary32

cases.golden_message: weight view 5: block scale application left the binary32 range
cases.name: matmul_fp8_scale_overflow
cases.note: a legal E8M0 code of 2**127 against the largest finite E4M3FN value: the scale application itself leaves the binary32 range

cases.name: vector_add_residual
cases.note: the residual add at a layer boundary: 6 x 64 BF16 through one binary32 rounding

cases.name: vector_add_saturating
cases.note: a sum that stays inside binary32 and leaves the BF16 range: the saturated value is reported and the saturation counted, on exactly the sixteen elements where it happens

cases.name: vector_add_exact_cancellation
cases.note: every element cancels exactly against its own negation, so every result is a zero whose sign the contract canonicalises

cases.golden_message: bf16_add_rne_v1: left_codes contains BF16 NaN or infinity
cases.name: vector_add_nonfinite
cases.note: an infinite residual operand is refused rather than propagated

cases.name: selection_argmax_dense
cases.note: 512 BF16 logits with one maximum: the token is the index of that maximum and the tie multiplicity is one

cases.name: selection_argmax_lowest_id_wins
cases.note: three logits share the maximum: greedy_lowest_token_id_argmax must select 17 and publish a tie multiplicity of three.  A comparison that replaced the running best on equality would select 201 and still look like a maximum

cases.name: selection_argmax_signed_zero_tie
cases.note: the maximum is zero and it appears as both +0 and -0.  They compare equal in binary32, so the token is the lower index and the tie multiplicity is two; a comparison keyed on the raw sign-magnitude pattern would rank -0 below +0 and get both wrong

cases.name: selection_argmax_binary32_partition
cases.note: a vocabulary partition that already produced binary32 logits, which the frozen rule reads without widening

cases.golden_message: selection logits view 2 contains a NaN or infinite value; a token may not be selected from it
cases.name: selection_argmax_nonfinite
cases.note: a NaN logit is a numeric fault: no token may be selected from it

cases.name: dma_gather_rows
cases.note: twelve rows gathered out of thirty-two, which is the shape every KV read and every routed-expert weight read takes

cases.name: dma_gather_repeated_index
cases.note: a repeated gather index is not an error: the same row is read twice

cases.name: dma_scatter_rows
cases.note: six rows written into a twenty-four-row destination whose other eighteen rows must survive unchanged.  The destination starts from real bytes, not zeros, so a datapath that forgot to read it back cannot pass

cases.name: dma_scatter_repeated_index_last_wins
cases.note: slot 0 and slot 4 name the same destination row: ascending slot order makes the later slot the one that survives, deterministically

cases.golden_message: DMA index view 2 names row 32, outside the 32 rows of the addressed view
cases.name: dma_gather_index_out_of_range
cases.note: an index one past the addressed extent: refused before anything moves, not clamped and not wrapped

cases.golden_message: DMA index view 2 names row 40, outside the 24 rows of the addressed view
cases.name: dma_scatter_index_out_of_range
cases.note: the same refusal on the write side, where a clamped index would corrupt a row nothing named

cases.name: vector_convert_bf16_to_fp32
cases.note: exact BF16 widening, including both signed-zero encodings and a subnormal; storage conversion must not inherit the arithmetic decoder's positive-zero canonicalisation

cases.name: vector_convert_fp32_to_bf16_rounding
cases.note: binary32-to-BF16 ties-to-even, ordinary rounding and a finite value that saturates at the BF16 storage boundary

cases.name: vector_convert_fp8_to_bf16
cases.note: E4M3FN codes widen through the exhaustive format decoder and cross one BF16 boundary

cases.golden_message: CONVERT source view 2 contains 1 NaN or infinite binary32 value(s)
cases.name: vector_convert_late_nonfinite
cases.note: the final binary32 source is infinity: the complete preflight must leave every earlier destination word untouched

cases.name: vector_convert_count_513_refused_by_rtl
cases.note: one element beyond the bounded RTL profile is refused before any destination word is written

cases.name: vector_scale_constant_eighth
cases.note: BF16 values multiplied by the profile's exact binary32 0.125 constant, with one binary32 product and one BF16 rounding

cases.name: vector_scale_constant_zero
cases.note: a zero scale remains the constant-scale sub-case because aux0, not scale_bits, selects the operation

cases.name: vector_scale_elementwise
cases.note: same-shape BF16 factors exercise signed products, cancellation and the elementwise aux0 selector

cases.name: vector_scale_saturating
cases.note: finite binary32 products beyond the BF16 range saturate and are counted instead of being mistaken for arithmetic overflow

cases.golden_message: SCALE source view 2 contains 1 NaN or infinite binary32 value(s)
cases.name: vector_scale_late_nonfinite
cases.note: a BF16 infinity in the final source position proves that buffered SCALE does not commit its valid prefix

cases.golden_message: SCALE source view 2 contains 1 NaN or infinite binary32 value(s)
cases.name: vector_scale_late_nonfinite_after_saturation
cases.note: the first finite result saturates but the final source is infinity; the refusal exposes neither writes nor the speculative saturation

cases.name: vector_hadamard_random_rows
cases.note: two seeded 128-wide BF16 rows cover every ascending-stride butterfly stage and the exact 1/sqrt(128) normalisation

cases.name: vector_hadamard_directed
cases.note: an impulse-and-cancellation row makes butterfly signs, zero canonicalisation and the normalisation constant independently visible

cases.golden_message: HADAMARD view 2 has width 64; the qualified transform is 128-point
cases.name: vector_hadamard_wrong_width
cases.note: a 64-point row is not silently treated as half a qualified transform

cases.golden_message: HADAMARD source view 2 contains 1 NaN or infinite binary32 value(s)
cases.name: vector_hadamard_late_nonfinite
cases.note: a NaN in the final element is found during the load preflight before any transformed row is committed

cases.name: vector_hadamard_five_rows_refused_by_rtl
cases.note: one row above the bounded four-row profile is refused

cases.name: vector_index_score_seeded
cases.note: the functional-test shape: two sites, four heads, five candidates and eight head channels, with every intermediate BF16 boundary

cases.name: vector_index_score_relu_tree
cases.note: directed positive and negative head dots expose the post-rounding ReLU and the balanced four-head reduction

cases.name: vector_index_score_exact_product_add
cases.note: the low exact-product bits of the second depth step round the head dot to 0x02be8001 and therefore BF16 0x02bf; a multiply-then-add implementation instead produces BF16 0x02be

cases.name: vector_index_score_weighted_saturation
cases.note: a finite weighted head score crosses the BF16 boundary and must increment the architectural vector.saturations event

cases.name: vector_index_score_qk_saturation
cases.note: the ordered QK dot remains finite but its BF16 boundary saturates and increments vector.saturations

cases.name: vector_index_score_output_saturation
cases.note: the balanced head sum remains binary32-finite but the final BF16 output boundary saturates and increments vector.saturations

cases.golden_message: INDEX_SCORE key view 4 contains BF16 NaN or infinity
cases.name: vector_index_score_late_nonfinite
cases.note: the last key channel is infinity; the three-operand preflight leaves all site/candidate scores untouched

cases.name: vector_compress_project_seeded
cases.note: three hidden rows project into distinct KV and gate planes under strictly ascending reduction order

cases.name: vector_compress_project_order
cases.note: catastrophic cancellation makes ascending reduction visible while deliberately different matrices make KV-then-gate plane order visible

cases.name: vector_compress_project_exact_product_add
cases.note: a depth-two projection whose exact-product single-rounded result is 0x0131b843; rounding the second product before adding produces the adjacent but incorrect 0x0131b842

cases.golden_message: COMPRESS_PROJECT gate projection view 6 contains BF16 NaN or infinity
cases.name: vector_compress_project_late_nonfinite
cases.note: a NaN in the final gate-weight element is rejected before either projection plane is committed

cases.name: vector_mhc_post_seeded
cases.note: two sites and four streams exercise the branch product, every combination coefficient and the balanced residual tree

cases.name: vector_mhc_post_matrix_order
cases.note: a nonsymmetric combination matrix distinguishes architectural comb[source][destination] addressing from its transpose

cases.name: vector_mhc_post_output_saturation
cases.note: one finite post-scaled branch crosses the BF16 output boundary; the output saturates to 0x7f7f and vector.saturations increments once

cases.golden_message: HYPER_CONNECT_POST combination view 8 contains a NaN or infinite binary32 value
cases.name: vector_mhc_post_late_nonfinite
cases.note: the last combination coefficient is NaN; four-operand preflight must preserve the entire residual-shaped destination

decode_reference: runtime.sim.formats E4M3FN_VALUES, MXFP4_VALUES and E8M0_VALUES, enumerated at import time from the exact fractions.Fraction decoders in runtime/reference/formats.py, plus runtime.sim.formats.widen_bf16

descriptor_admission.derivation: each case record derives arity, every input/output dtype, rank and dimension, scaled state, numeric profile fields, complete contract digest and aux bindings independently from the admitted deployment descriptors
descriptor_admission.negative_policy: negative cases alter one derived record field after derivation and require ERR_SHAPE with no result or speculative saturation count

engine_policy: no engine is stubbed: every case is executed by runtime.sim.device.Device with the real implementations in runtime.sim.engines, and the operand and result images are read back out of device memory after the transaction

numeric_reference.bf16_bf16_fp32_sequential_rne_v1: runtime.tensor_accelerator.bf16.dense_bf16_linear_bf16 for BF16 x BF16 -> BF16; runtime.sim.backend.sequential_matmul_binary32 for every other operand pair
numeric_reference.bf16_mul_rne_v1_and_bf16_scale_rne_v1: runtime.sim.engines.vector._vector_scale using the selected backend's binary32 multiply and one output conversion
numeric_reference.unscaled_convert_one_input_one_output: runtime.sim.engines.vector._vector_convert using runtime.sim.formats widen/narrow; identity dtypes are copied
